name: Iron Beam 100 kW laser (Rafael)
description: Rafael Iron Beam ('Or Eitan'), 100 kW-class laser handed to the Israeli Air Force 28 Dec 2025: the first high-energy laser air-defence system declared operationally mature. Reported to burn rockets, mortars and UAS at about 10 km in clear air; interception takes seconds. Fires from a static emplacement and degrades badly in cloud, fog and low visibility, which is why Iron Dome remains the all-weather layer.

maxRangeM.note: Inventory records 10000 m (10 km); the seed value is kept

engageTimeS.condition: dwell time to effect — An Israeli defence official said 'the interception takes seconds'. A separate lower-tier report gives about five seconds. Five is used as the representative reading of 'seconds'; it is target-dependent and not a published threshold.
engageTimeS.source: Breaking Defense, 'Lasers in the field: Iron Beam clears last test before operational use'

outputPowerKw.condition: 100 kW-class laser with a 10 km engagement envelope
outputPowerKw.source: Army Recognition, AUSA 2025 Iron Beam report

beamQualityM2.note: Planning factor: no high-energy laser programme publishes a beam quality. Open optics references put high-power multimode and combined-fibre beams at M squared of about 1.5 to 3; 2.0 is the planning value for every laser in the library. Rafael says the beam director uses coherent beam combination and adaptive optics and publishes no beam quality.

jitterUrad.note: Planning factor: no high-energy laser programme publishes a pointing jitter. The Airborne Laser Laboratory of the 1980s held about 25 urad and modern beam control is better, so 10 urad at 1 sigma is the planning value for every laser in the library.

apertureM.note: Planning factor: no high-energy laser programme publishes a beam director aperture. Open beam-director literature describes 30 to 50 cm apertures for weapon-class systems; 0.30 m is the planning value for every laser in the library. The Rafael claim of a coin-sized spot at 10 km would imply an aperture nearer 1 m if taken literally, so 0.30 m is the conservative end for this system.

dwellToEffectS.condition: reported burn-through in 2 to 5 s at up to 10 km; the lower bound is taken
dwellToEffectS.source: Defense Update, Iron Beam 450 report, 17 September 2025, quoted from the search index; the page returned HTTP 403 on read
dwellToEffectS.note: The 2 to 5 s figure is quoted for the Iron Beam 450 beam director against rockets, mortars and UAS, not specifically against a Group 1 quadcopter, and Rafael's own material says only that the system dwells for seconds. Treat it as the order of magnitude, not a measured dwell.
